properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 26 at 12:07AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon.
Relative humidity values are forecast to drop into the 30 to 40
percent range, especially near and north of the Interstate 10 and
12 corridors. The 20 ft wind forecast is expected to remain at or
below 10 mph in most areas, which should limit critical fire
weather conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that
may ignite.

Numerous local burn bans are in place across LA and MS due to
ongoing drought conditions. Outdoor burning is strongly
discouraged as the ongoing drought conditions continue, and all
local restrictions should be followed.

properties.description:
TOREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Northwestern Hudspeth County in western Texas...

* Until 1115 PM MDT.

* At 1045 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a
tornado was located 4 miles south of Desert Haven, moving east at
20 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This tornadic thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
northwestern Hudspeth County.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 8:19PM AKDT until October 28 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 1 to 2.5 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 30 to 40 mph southwest
winds with gusts up to 40 to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT Wednesday, highest water levels expected
during each upcoming high tide through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady south to southwesterly flow is
expected to continue for the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through
Wednesday morning as a series of low pressure systems track
across the Bering Sea. Coastal erosion and minor coastal
flooding will be possible with each upcoming high tide due to
the persistent onshore winds, during which maximum water levels
will reach between 1 and 2.5 ft above the normal highest tide
line, including in and around Kipnuk and Kwigillingok. The
strong winds may reduce the ability for flood waters to recede
during and close to low tide, possibly leading to prolonged
higher than normal water levels along the coast and near the
mouth of the Kuskokwim River. There will be a break in strong
winds between Wednesday afternoon and Thursday morning,
however, we are monitoring the potential for another strong
storm system that could cause additional coastal impacts towards
the end of this week.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 8:36PM PDT until October 29 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San Francisco
Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 11:39 AM
Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43
PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up to 1.0 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
